title: Done means delivered
subtitle: A result counts as delivered only after it has been written to the receiver's socket, and polling a job costs what is ready rather than what is pending
technologies: Idempotency, exactly-once effects and crash recovery

stats.label: rebuilds every result after a restart
set once per connection scopes every poll

lede: The input side of my broker is told in Millions of queued items that were not there: two-phase dispatch and in-place tombstones made the count of tokens received equal the count routed, to the token. The output side had the same disease in mirror image. A result could be marked finished, handed to a poller, and lost between the broker's memory and the receiver's hands. So the completion side got the same discipline, and polling got a data structure that scales with what is ready. Results from the GPUs are written to completion segments, append-only files. Recovery after a restart is a scan of those segments, so a result that reached disk is never forgotten by a crash.
quote: A result can be re-offered, and it is never silently gone.
evidence: Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: a result counts as delivered only after it is flushed to the receiver's socket and confirmed, so a receiver that dies is offered the same results again.
Append-only log design: results written to completion segments that 1 scan rebuilds after a restart, with a committed offset as the readable boundary.
Message broker and queue design: a job id set once per connection and job-scoped ready queues, so a poll costs what is ready rather than the whole pending backlog.
author: Corey James
